chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him), who said:
I asked him about a man who marries a woman, then marries the mother of his concubine (from a previous marriage), he said, 'There is no harm in that.'

key_terms.أُمَّ وَلَدٍ: Mother of a concubine; a female slave who bears her master a child, gaining specific legal status.
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: There is no harm; a common juristic phrase indicating permissibility or lack of prohibition.
key_terms.يَتَزَوَّجُ: He marries; refers to the act of contracting a marriage.

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible in Shia Islam for a man to marry the mother of his concubine?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Rida (AS), the permissibility of marrying the mother of one's concubine (umm al-walad) is confirmed, highlighting the flexibility of Shia jurisprudence regarding marital unions beyond the standard four-wife limit. This ruling underscores the distinct treatment of concubinage in classical fiqh, where the mother of a child by a slave woman holds a specific status that allows for subsequent marriage to her. The hadith serves as a foundational text for understanding the legal mechanisms of polygyny and concubinage in the context of early Islamic society.
